seo.title: FLUX 3 Video Draft Generator for 720p Iteration
seo.description: Create 720p FLUX 3 Draft trials with text, images or timed keyframes, retain native Extend, and enhance eligible owned paired Drafts with a separate quote.

overview: FLUX 3 Video Draft creates 720p text, image, first-and-last-frame and timed-keyframe trials and retains native Draft Extend. Enhance is a separate 1080p operation for an eligible owned native Draft with a qualified paired cache. A successful Draft does not guarantee an available cache. Black Forest Labs owns FLUX; MaxVideoAI distributes this model through Fal.

hero.title: FLUX 3 Video Draft
hero.subtitle: Native 720p Draft with keyframes and Extend; separate Enhance for eligible paired Drafts.
hero.paragraph: Use native Draft at 720p for text, image, two-frame, timed-keyframe and Extend trials. Enhance re-renders an eligible owned native Draft at 1080p from its paired cache; imports, copied public videos and Draft Extend caches cannot supply that eligibility. The earlier Draft charge remains separate.

features.title: Fixed 720p iteration
features.body: Native Draft stays at 720p. Eligible paired-cache Enhance is separately quoted at 1080p; it does not make every Draft automatically enhanceable.

features.title: Same explicit source roles
features.body: Text needs a prompt, image mode needs an opening image, first-last-frame needs both anchors, keyframes needs 1–10 indexed images, and native Extend needs a source video.

features.title: Fast creative decisions
features.body: Use short controlled scenes to compare camera direction, action timing and visual continuity. Avoid spending the draft loop on several unrelated story beats that cannot be diagnosed.

features.title: Draft extension remains separate
features.body: Native Draft Extend remains a 720p continuation workflow with its own quote. Its cache is not eligible for Enhance.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: controlled 720p trials
decisionCards.body: Use Draft for early frame bridges, source-video continuation tests, motion sketches and prompt comparisons with one measurable change per attempt.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: final production equivalence
decisionCards.body: Native Draft stays at 720p. Eligible paired-cache Enhance is separately quoted at 1080p; it does not make every Draft automatically enhanceable.

decisionCards.title: Design tests that transfer
decisionCards.body: Keep source frames, prompt structure and acceptance criteria reusable so the successful draft can be evaluated consistently on the standard model.

referenceWorkflows.title: Text sketch
referenceWorkflows.body: Test one scene idea with a clear action, camera path and ending.

referenceWorkflows.title: Image sketch
referenceWorkflows.body: Animate an opening frame while preserving subject and composition.

referenceWorkflows.title: Frame-bridge sketch
referenceWorkflows.body: Use two compatible anchors and specify the plausible transition between them.

referenceWorkflows.title: Extension sketch
referenceWorkflows.body: Continue an eligible source clip without resetting identity, camera or light.

referenceWorkflows.title: Keyframes
referenceWorkflows.body: Use 1–10 ordered images and unique frame positions from 0 through requested seconds × 24. Choose 5–20 whole seconds; first-and-last-frame mode still requires both anchors.

referenceWorkflows.title: Enhance Draft
referenceWorkflows.body: Enhance requires your own completed native text, image, first-last-frame or keyframe Draft and a verified paired cache. Not every Draft supplies one. Measured source duration must be positive and at most 21 seconds; this is an application admission limit, not a provider output guarantee. Availability is checked again before execution; enhancement has its own quote.

tabNotes.body: A draft is valuable when it reduces one concrete uncertainty, even if it is not a final asset.
Keep first-last-frame separate from 1–10 indexed keyframes. Enhance requires your own eligible native Draft and a qualified paired cache, not just an exported MP4.
Record sources, prompt and acceptance notes before switching to standard FLUX 3.

globalPrinciples: Change one major variable per draft.
Use sources that are compatible in identity and scene logic.
Keep movement physically readable at short duration.
Apply rights, consent and safety review even to temporary outputs.
engineWhy: Text needs a prompt, image mode needs an opening image, first-last-frame needs both anchors, keyframes needs 1–10 indexed images, and native Extend needs a source video.
Native Draft Extend remains a 720p continuation workflow with its own quote. Its cache is not eligible for Enhance.
Separate extension pricing prevents a draft continuation from being quoted as ordinary generation.

demo.title: FLUX 3 Draft continuation test
demo.prompt: Continue the supplied clip from its final frame: the small research boat keeps moving left to right through low morning fog while the camera maintains the same slow aerial track. A buoy passes beneath the frame and the wake widens naturally. Preserve hull colors, crew count, horizon height and cool light. Do not introduce a cut, title, logo or new vessel.
notes: The prompt begins from the source clip's ending state.
Continuity anchors make the draft useful for standard-model handoff.
